subject: Request: Trial top-up for dataset curation pilot / IRB delay

messages:
From: Dr. Amara N'diaye <amara@umb.edu>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, Sep 1, 2028 at 09:12 AM -0700
Subject: Trial top-up request for dataset curation pilot (IRB delay)

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the initial credits to kick off our dataset curation pilot with Redwood. We've run into an unexpected delay: the university IRB has requested an addendum for our de-identification procedures, which pushed our start back by ~3 weeks. Because of the delay and the additional annotation passes we now need, could North Bay University request an extension or supplemental trial credit?

Quick context: this is a non-commercial, faculty-led research project focused on building a cleaned, de-identified corpus of municipal records for public-interest research. Estimated incremental usage if approved: ~150k tokens over 6 weeks (mostly embedding + light generation for QA).

I've attached the IRB approval (redacted), updated dataset scope, and a data sensitivity matrix. We are a modest lab — any promo extension or voucher that lets us complete the annotation round would be a huge help. We can provide the project page and an institutional letter if required.

Next steps we need from Redwood: 1) confirmation if an extension or supplemental credit is possible for academic pilots; 2) any forms/POs required; 3) estimated timeline for provisioning so we can plan the annotation schedule.

Appreciate your help,

—Amara
Dr. Amara N'diaye
Principal Investigator, Data Curation Lab
North Bay University
[data-curation-lab@northbay.edu]

Attachments: IRB_approval_redacted.pdf (pdf), dataset_scope_v2.docx (docx), sensitivity_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Amara N'diaye <amara@umb.edu>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, Sep 1, 2028 at 09:40 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Trial top-up request for dataset curation pilot (IRB delay)

Hi Amara — thanks for the note and for sending the IRB/redacted docs. I've looped in Marissa (research partnerships) and Ben (education programs) so we can review quickly. A few clarifying questions to make the approval faster:  

- Confirmed start window after IRB: you mentioned ~3 weeks; what is the new target start date?
- Can you estimate monthly token profile (embeddings vs generation) — e.g., 100k embeddings / 50k generation?
- Will any data be uploaded to Private deployments or processed via our hosted API? (We ask to advise on retention policy.)

As a provisional measure, we can provision a temporary 50k-token promo top-up pending program review, but final augmentation will depend on risk review and whether you need an extended trial longer than 6 weeks. If you're able to send a short institutional letter (PDF) confirming non-commercial research use and PI contact, that will speed approvals.

I'll coordinate internally and mark this as a high-priority academic pilot request. Ben/Marissa — any initial thoughts on additional credits or standard paperwork?

Best,

Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
Phone: (415) 555-0182

Attachment placeholders referenced by client: IRB_approval_redacted.pdf, dataset_scope_v2.docx

From: Dr. Amara N'diaye <amara@umb.edu>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, Sep 1, 2028 at 10:07 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Trial top-up request for dataset curation pilot (IRB delay)

Thanks Irene — answers below and attaching the institutional letter you requested.

- New target start date: 2028-09-24 (projected annotation kickoff week).
- Token profile (estimated for the six-week window): ~120k embeddings (sentence-level), ~30k generation tokens (QA prompts and cleanup).
- Hosting: We'll use the hosted API for the initial annotation workflow; we do not require Private deployment for this pilot. We will request a short retention window (30 days) during preprocessing and then export cleaned assets.

Attached: NBU_research_letter_signed.pdf (institutional letter confirming non-commercial PI-led research).

If 50k tokens can be provisioned now as a provisional top-up, that would let us pilot one annotation batch and confirm the runbook before the main ingestion. Happy to hop on a 20-min call if that helps.

—Amara

Hi Amara — welcome, and thanks for the thorough package. We've reviewed the IRB redaction, the sensitivity matrix, and NBU's institutional letter.

We're happy to grant a provisional 50k-token promo credit to North Bay University's pilot to get you through the first annotation pass. Next steps:

- Irene / Marissa: please create a voucher code tied to account "North Bay University - Data Curation Lab" (HubSpot deal DB-98765) and set expiry to 2028-11-01.
- Amara: we'll need the email address to attach the voucher to (please confirm which email will redeem it).
- Legal/Billing: if additional tokens become necessary beyond the provisional top-up, we'll follow the education supplement approval path and formalize via a short MSA amendment or PO.

Marissa — can you own the voucher issuance and confirmation to Amara? Irene — please add me to any follow-up for quota increases.

Congrats on moving past the IRB. Looking forward to seeing initial results.

Best,

Ben Carter
Head, Education Programs — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
